options.text: Smoke particles move freely in all directions with negligible attractions, so the smoke spreads to fill the available space.
Smoke particles stay tightly packed like the solid incense stick, so the smoke keeps one fixed shape and one fixed volume.
The smoke spreads through the cupboard first, and that spreading then causes free motion of its particles.
The same explanation applies to the solid incense stick itself, not only to the smoke gas.

stem:
Ira lights an incense stick in one corner of a closed cupboard. Soon the smoke spreads through the whole cupboard and fills every gap.

Why does this gas have no fixed shape or fixed volume?

teacher.key_rationale: Gas particles move freely with negligible attractions, so a gas has no fixed shape or volume and fills available space.
